page.layout: One page of verse, one block of lines in the centre; running head at the top with page number at left; a partial line "Hæc" at the lower right of the text block. No margin notes.

main_text.p:
Nati, Guisiadas, fatalia nomina, dixit,
Arcete vestris finibus.

Exitio crescent vestro, populiq; ruinis
Tollent caput superbum

O mala quanta ferent, audaces funera quanta
Genti mouebunt francicæ!

Non patriæ flammas, Helenem quæ duxit adulter
Damnosiores intulit.

Non dedit Ausoniæ graviora incommoda dirus
Carthaginensis Annibal.

Hæc igitur memores prædicta revoluite, Galli,
Quæ tristis euentus probat.

Et vestris tandem satiati cladibus, atqʒ
Luctu ruentis patriæ:

Non fraude, ast Francùm vera virtute superbi,
Malis carere quærite.

Magnates veterum cretos de sanguine Regum, &
Gallos fouete nobiles.

Gallos Gallus amat, pro Rege perire paratus,
Pro chariore Patria.

Ad fines verum si spes deducet auara
Vestros vagantes hospites,

Excipere ignotos solita leuitate cauete,
Cauete fraudes exteras.

Indigenas Gallos nunquam hospes auarus ambit,
Sibi suisq; proximus.

Proditione, dolis, scelere, atqʒ libidine, & ira,
Opes parabit impias.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s. Line breaks within verses shown as br; the printed verse lines are indented, so each stanza is one paragraph. Hæc at lower right is a catchword-like fragment; treated as a line of text. Some words in the italic verse are uncertain (e.g. "Guisiadas", "Ausoniæ") but read as printed.
